method: Static decoding, AST and LNK field tracing; isolated evaluator captures with process/network functions stubbed. No live payload retrieval or host command execution.

evidence: The two replaceAll operations are no-ops: the Base64 literal contains neither replacement character.
Buffer.from(..., base64).toString(utf8) produces a child_process.exec expression, immediately executed through Function(...)().
The shell command captures whole lines from a Finger user@host query and uses the same FOR variable as the command to execute; START requests minimization.
An isolated JavaScript evaluator with stubbed Buffer/require/exec captured the reconstructed command without launching a process.
runtime_limits: The endpoint is relay.example; no functioning external service is established.
Function evaluates in global scope and requires a global require; ordinary CommonJS-local require is insufficient.
Final remote commands, deployment authorization and provenance are unavailable. No malware-family attribution is justified.
samples.basis: The concealed remote-output-to-command path and minimized launch support likely malicious staging; operational reachability is not asserted.

evidence: Literal replacement restores Cyrillic characters to E and D in a Base64-encoded Python program.
Module-level exec runs the decoded source, which imports urllib.request and passes urlopen(...).read() directly to exec.
The URL uses unauthenticated HTTP; there is no signature, integrity check, confirmation or useful visible application behavior.
A closed import map and fake response confirmed the URL and the response-bytes-to-exec relationship without network access.
runtime_limits: The response and downstream payload were not retrieved.
Provenance and authorized deployment context are unavailable.
The analyzer does not reconstruct this Unicode substitution layer; two suspicious traits describe the justified static evidence without inventing downstream behavior.
samples.basis: Concealed unconditional execution of arbitrary HTTP response bytes supports likely malicious staging.

samples.identification: Incomplete Windows shortcut and inert Startup-script ZIP
evidence: ZIP has exactly two members, launch.lnk and stage.txt; there is no inner.zip, settings.ini or runnable extracted payload.
The LNK flags are 0xa0 (arguments and Unicode). It has no target ID list, LinkInfo, relative target or executable target. ShowCommand is zero.
Its arguments describe a headless conhost/cmd tar extraction, config-to-batch copy and batch invocation, but those arguments alone cannot establish a usable shortcut.
The unlinked stage.txt would write only @echo off into a Startup batch file if manually interpreted as batch. It installs no functional payload.
There is no established theft, surveillance, destruction, backdoor or user deception in the supplied bytes.
runtime_limits: A working target, missing inner archive and separate deployment instructions could change the assessment; none were supplied.
samples.basis: Incomplete command carrier and inert script do not justify conviction or hostile persistence traits.

trait_changes: Accept escaped apostrophes in Finger FOR-variable binding, preserving case-sensitive variable equality; accept escaped START title quotes and usebackq exclusions.
Add bound Unicode-substitution-to-Base64-to-exec detection and neutral character substitution observations.
Recognize immediate Function(...)() as well as new Function(...)() execution.
Reduce Base64 plus Function construction from hostile to suspicious; generic Buffer/atob-to-Function construction is neutral generation.
Move decoded require and eval syntax into metadata/lang/source/syntax/call; decoded child_process spelling into metadata/import/builtin.

Remove the redundant encoded cmd.exe observation and use the canonical executable-name reference in its two consumers. These consumers now accept plain or decoded cmd.exe references; their other required resource/registry/process context remains.
Split neutral Base64/evaluation proximity by direct versus constructed execution; construction without invocation no longer satisfies constructed evaluation.

Move START minimization and its Finger-query context to ui/window/state; move inline child_process member syntax to metadata/lang/source/syntax/member. Broad process-create selectors consequently no longer count these non-launch observations.
A direct require token no longer triggers the helper-module-name rule; zero-switch Finger queries use the canonical user@host matcher.
Neutral decoded module and inline member observations retain no bundle, test-path or product suppressions: these contexts do not invalidate a syntax/reference claim.
controls: cases.json and check.py: positive substitutions, no-op/ASCII/unrelated replacement negatives, escaped and ordinary Finger commands, variable case mismatch, usebackq literal input, echo-only body, Function construction versus invocation.
